aria: Animated recap of the Suns' 123 to 119 overtime road win over the Pelicans: Devin Booker's step-back jumper with 31 seconds left in regulation that made it 109 to 107, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Jalen Green's 25 points, the top scorers, how the Suns won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from the Suns' 123–119 overtime road win over the New Orleans Pelicans on Nov 23, 2026, from the Covers box score; all 123 Phoenix points and all 119 New Orleans points add up from the player lines. The quarter scores (31–25–23–30, OT 14, to 35–19–29–26, OT 10) add up to both totals: Phoenix led 56–54 at the half (AP; Crescent City Sports), New Orleans led 83–79 after three (Crescent City Sports), and it was 109–109 after regulation (AP). Shooting (Phoenix 44 of 91, 15 of 39 from three, 20 of 27 FT; New Orleans 45 of 101, 11 of 32, 18 of 26), assists (28–27), blocks (5–3), points in the paint (44–62), offensive rebounds (9–17) and the biggest leads (Phoenix 7, New Orleans 10) are from Covers; Arizona Sports also gives the 62 paint points, the 17 offensive rebounds, Phoenix's 13 steals and the 67–39 bench edge for New Orleans, and Crescent City Sports also says New Orleans led by as many as 10. Player lines used here also match the AP (Green 25, Booker 22, Gillespie 18; Poole 28 with 6 of 8 from three, Williamson 25, Bey 21). Miles Bridges' 14 points are from the Covers box score, which adds up to 123; the AP says 13. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Monday's games.

Phoenix won its fourth straight and handed New Orleans its fourth straight loss; the Pelicans have lost 10 of 11 since a 4-4 start (AP). Jordan Poole made his first nine shots and scored all 28 of his points in the first three quarters, a season high (AP; Crescent City Sports). Collin Gillespie scored five of his 18 in overtime (AP) and 12 in the fourth quarter and overtime (Arizona Sports). Next: Phoenix plays at Houston on Wednesday in the NBA Cup; New Orleans plays at the Clippers on Friday (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Devin Booker's step-back jumper: AP: "Phoenix also led 109-107 with 31 seconds left in regulation after Booker's step-back jumper." A two-point jumper, so the board's Tied to Suns +2 is 107–107 to 109–107. Jordan Fears' driving scoop tied it at 109 with 22.8 seconds left and Herb Jones stole Booker's pass at the end of regulation (AP); Phoenix pulled away in overtime with a 10–4 run (AP). The clock runs from 0:34 to 0:31 for the animation; only the 31 seconds is reported. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Phoenix Suns or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Devin Booker's listed 6-foot-5 and 206 pounds (Basketball-Reference; Wikipedia) with No. 15, the number he switched to for 2026-27 (Cronkite News), and his arms are scaled to a 6-foot-8¼ wingspan measured at the 2015 draft combine (Tankathon). He is drawn in Phoenix's road colors with his proposed look from the site's look sheet (not yet approved). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
